text: Yila Yesu wekalaa kuu nthi niwatavisye atume make iulu wa ituni. Eita itu "Musyi wa asa wakwa," na wina mawikalo maingi muno. Mawikalo ni musyi munene mwanake. Itu ni inene na niyanake muno na kuyaoneka musyi mwanake tusu kuu nthi.
translation:
When Jesus lived on earth He told His disciples about Heaven.
He called it "My Father's House",
and said there were many mansions there.
A mansion is a large, beautiful home.
Heaven is larger and more beautiful than any earthly home.

text: Yesu asyaa, "ninanthi kumuseuvisya vandu na namina kumuseuvisya ngoka ingi nimwisie." Yesu niwambatie ituni yila wathayukie kuma kwa akwu. Atume make masyaisye, Yesu niwoosiwe ambatwa iulu ituni na matuni nimamwosie na maeka umwona.
translation:
Jesus said,
"I go to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you,
I will come again and receive you to Myself."
Jesus did go to Heaven,
after He arose from the dead.
While His disciples watched,
Jesus was taken up,
and a cloud received Him out of
their sight.

text:
Kuma ivinda yiu, akilisto nimalilikana Yesu. Ameei kana akooka ingi kumesia. Aisye kana akooka ta kingie. Lakini kukethya kuilyi ata kwa ala makusaa atokiti? Mbivilia nitutavitye kana maendaa imwe imwe kwithiwa na Ngai. Kwithiwa mwii utevo ni kwithiwa wivo
Kwithiwa na vala ve Mwiai.
translation:
Since then,
Christians have remembered Jesus' promise to come back and get them.
Jesus said He would return suddenly,
when least expected.
But what about Christians who die before He comes?
The Bible says they go straight to be with Jesus.
To be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord.

text: Uvuanwo, ivuku ya mwiso ya mbivilia, yitutavasya undi itu yanakavite. Kwa kitumi ki mwanya itu niyo musyi wa Ngai. Ngai ekila vandu na usumbi wake wi ituni.
translation:
Revelation, the last book in the Bible,
tells us how wonderful Heaven is.
The most wonderful thing is that,
in a very special way, Heaven is God's home.
God is everywhere, but His throne is in Heaven.

text: Alaika na syumbe ila ingi syi ituni nimukumasya na kumuthaitha Ngai. Kwa kwika ouu, andu onthe ma Ngai ala makwie na mathi ituni maina mbathi nzeo sya kumatia Ngai.
translation:
Angels and other heavenly beings worship God in Heaven.
So do all God's people who have died and gone to Heaven.
They sing special songs of praise to God.

text: Vaa ve ndeto sya wathi umwe mainie: We wiwa lato nene nundu niwatwovoisye kula kwi Ngai na thakame yaku kuma kila mbai na nthi syonthe na niwatutwikithisye asumbi na athembi kula kwi Ngai waitu. (UVuanwo 5:9).
translation:
Here are some words from one song they sing.
YOU ARE WORTHY FOR YOU HAVE REDEEMED US TO GOD BY YOUR BLOOD OUT OF EVERY TRIBE AND
NATION AND HAVE
MADE US KINGS
AND PRIESTS
TO OUR GOD.
(
Rev. 5:9
)

text: Ithangu ya muthya ya mbivilia yielietye itu ta, "Yelusalemu nzau". Ni inene, inene muno yina ukuta mutulu nza, ukuta wakwitwe na mavia malumu meukengakenga ta ngenyingenyi sya uakangani.
translation:
The very last pages of the Bible describe Heaven as "The New Jerusalem".
It is very,
very big,
with a high wall outside.
The wall is of jasper stone,
clear as crystal.

text: Masoa na mavia matheu meutisatisa mavyikite musingi wa ukuta, wina
translation:
Jewels and precious stones cover the foundation of the wall,
sparkling with gorgeous colors.

text: malangi makundu na kila muvea wa musyi useuvitwe na miomo minene ya thaavu.
translation: Each of the city gates is made of a single huge pearl!

text: Miomo isu minene ya thaavu ndi vingawa. Tuthi nthini tukeeloele. Mwanye!! Itu kau niyanake muno ou nthini!!!! Musyi usu wakitwe na thaavu muthei, ta kioo kitheu, ona nzia syakitwe na tahhavu.
translation:
Those great pearly gates are never closed.
Let's go in and have a look around...WOW!
Heaven is even more beautiful inside.
The city is made of pure gold,
like clear glass.
Even the street is made of gold.

text: Mbusi ntheu sya kiwu kya thayu kyumite kivilani kya Ngai. Na kila ngaliko ya usi veethwaa kiti kya thayu, kila mbee kyoonikanite mundane wa eden. Uu ni muti wa mwanya. Usyaa mithemba ikumi na ili ya matunda, kivathukanwo kila mwei. Na matu ma muti usu wa thayu nimatumikaa kuvosya nthi syonthe.
translation:
A beautiful,
clear river of the water of life flows from God's throne.
On either side of the river is the tree of life,
which was first found in the Garden of Eden.
This tree is very special.
It bears twelve different kinds of fruit,
a different kind each month.
And the leaves of the tree of life are for the healing of the nations.

text: Ituni kuyendaa sua kana mwai kwona kyeni. Ngai niwe mwene ukumyo ula usuasya kyeni kitheu vau vai utuku ona umwe.
translation:
Heaven does not need the sun or moon for light.
God's own glory fills it with wonderful light.
There is never any night there.

text: Ona nyamu ituni nisya kivathukanyo muno syonthe ni mbuu na nisyendanite. Mbiwa na tulondu syiisya nyeki vamwe. Ona munyambu mukie muno uisaa vamwe na ngombe sya mulau. Na Mwia aasya, "iikaumanwa kana kwananga iima syake ntheu."
translation:
Even the animals in Heaven are different.
They are all tame and friendly.
Wolves and lambs feed on grass together.
Even mighty lions are eating straw like the ox.
The LORD says,
"They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain."

text: Tuisisya kila ngaliko, nitwona syindu itevo ituni. Ndukewa ndeto nthuku, vai mundu ukita na ungi kana kwiyenda.
translation:
As we look around,
we notice that there are things missing from Heaven.
No angry words are ever heard.
Nobody is fighting or being selfish.

text: Vai ivuli miomoni nundu kui ingei ituni. Vai akengani, owani, aoi, na andu angi athuku. Vai thavu ituni.
translation:
There are no locks on the doors,
because there are no thieves in Heaven.
There are no liars,
murderers,
sorcerers,
or other wicked people.
There is no sin of any kind in Heaven.

text: Twina Ngai ituni kuikethiwa methoi ingi. Mavinda amwe andu ma Ngai nimaia nundu wa woo mwingi wa maisha ma nthi ino. Kuya ituni Ngai akavangula methoi oonthe.
translation:
In Heaven with God there are no more tears.
Sometimes,
God's people cry because of great sorrows in this life.
In Heaven,
God will wipe away all tears.

text: Kui kikwu ituni. Andu ma Ngai makekela tene na tene vamwe nake. Vaikethwa kiio, Kiwoyo kya ngoo, na kuikethwa woo. Kuikethwa mauwau, kutiwa, na mathiko. Kila mundu ituni akewaa muyo vamwe na Ngai.
translation:
There is no death in Heaven,
either.
God's people will be forever with the Lord.
There is no more sorrow,
no more crying,
no more pain.
No sickness,
no parting,
no funerals.
Everyone in Heaven is happy forever with God.

text: Useo ula wivo, uu ni imwana na eitu (ona andu ala aima) ala mamuikiie Ngai ta mwiai woo na kuatiia miao yake. Kuya ituni kwi ivuku yitawa ivuku ya thayu.
translation:
Best of all,
Heaven is for boys and girls (and grown-ups too) who have believed on Jesus Christ as their Saviour and have obeyed Him as their Lord.

text: Yusiite masyitwa ma andu. Niwisi masyitwa ala maandikitwe vau? Ni masyitwa ma andu ala meekie wikwatyo woo vala ve Yesu. Isyitwa yaku ni vau?
translation:
In Heaven there is a book called the Lamb's Book of Life.
It is full of people's names.
Do you know whose names are written there?
All the people who put their trust in Jesus.
Is your name there?

text: Ndeto sya muthya sya Mbivilia ni kuthokwa kwa mwanya. "Na veva na mutwawa masya, 'Ukai!!' na ula wiiwa ni asye, 'uka' na ula wina wauni oke, oke ose kiwu kya thayu mana."
translation:
The Bible's last words about Heaven are a wonderful invitation.
"And the Spirit and the bride say,
'Come!'
And let him who hears say 'Come!'
And let him who thirsts come.
And whosoever desires,
let him take the water of life freely."

text:
Ituni musyi mwanake wa Ngai
Ngewa kuma kwa ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia
Yonekanaa
Yohana 14; 2 Akolintho 5; Uvuanwo 4, 21, 22
"Kulika kwa ndeto yaku kũetae kyeni."
Savulĩ 119:130
translation:
Heaven,
God's Beautiful Home
A story from God's Word,
the Bible,
is found in
John 14;
2 Corinthians 5;
Revelation 6, 21, 22
"
The entrance of Your Words gives light.
"
Psalm 119:130

text: Muthya
translation: The End

text:
Ngewa ino ya Mbivilia ĩtutavasya yiũlu wa Ngai witu wa ũseny'o ũla watumbie na ũla wendaa ũmumanye.
Ngai niwisi kana nitwikite maũndũ mathũku ala we ũmetaa naĩ. Usilĩlo wa naĩ ni kĩkw'ũ, indĩ Ngai nũtwendete mũno nũndũ nĩwatũmie mwana wake ũmwe, Yesu Klisto akw'e mũkelany'oni na asilĩlwa nũndũ wa naĩ syaku. Na ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwasyũkie na asyoka ĩtunĩ ĩngĩ! Ethĩwa nũũmũĩkĩĩa Yesu na ũimũkũlya akũekee nai syaku, nũkwĩka ũũ! Nũkũka na akĩkala nthĩnĩ wakũ yu, na ũkekala nake tene na tene.
Ethĩwa nũĩkĩĩa kana ũu niw'o, neene ndeto ii kwa Ngai: "Yesũ mwendwa, nĩngũĩkĩĩa kana wĩ Ngai ũla watwĩkĩe mundũ, akwa kwoondũ wa naĩ syakwa, nayu ni wikalaa thayũ ĩngĩ. Mwa, ũka thayũnĩ wakwa na ũindekea naĩ syakwa nikana mũthenya ũmwe nĩthi ĩtunĩ nĩthĩwe naku tene na tene. Ndethye nĩkwĩw'ae we na ndyikalaa naku ta kana kaku". Ameni.
Somaa Mbivilia na kũneenaa na Ngai kila mũthenya! Yoana 3:16
translation:
This Bible story tells us about our wonderful God who made us and who wants us to know Him.
God knows we have done bad things,
which He calls sin.
The punishment for sin is death,
but God loves us so much He sent His Son,
Jesus,
to die on a Cross and be punished for our sins.
Then Jesus came back to life and went home to Heaven!
If you believe in Jesus and ask Him to forgive your sins,
He will do it!
He will come and live in you now,
and you will live with Him forever.
If you want to turn from your sins,
say this to God:
Dear God,
I believe that Jesus died for me and now lives again.
Please come into my life and forgive my sins,
so that I can have a new life now,
and one day go to be with You forever.
Help me to live for You as your child.
Amen.
Read the Bible and talk with God every day!
John 3:16

text: Na kiveti kyaungamite ngaliko ya kiima cha kiio kinene kingi. Metho make ma tei masyaitwe iulu kwa visa muthuku. Mwana wake aendee na kukwa. Na kiveti kiu ni malia na kyaungamite vakuvia na vala Yesu wakuniwa misumaa ngelanyoni.
translation:
The lady stood on the noisy hillside,
her sad eyes looking up to a terrible scene.
Her Son was dying.
The mother was Mary,
and she stood near the place where Jesus was nailed to a cross.

text: Maundu asu meethiiwe ata? Kutonyeka ata Yesu akamina thayu wake kwisila nzia isu? Ngai atonya kwitikila ata mwana wake akwe ngelanyoni? Yesu niweekie nai kwithwa ee ula wai Ngai? Ngai nivulaukaa?
translation:
How did all this happen?
How could Jesus end such a beautiful life in such an awful way?
How could God allow His Son to be nailed to a cross to die there?
Did Jesus make a mistake about Who He was?
Did God fail?

text: Ayee Ngai ndavaluka! Ngai ndaika ivityo ona yimwe! Yesu niweesi akowawa ni andu ala matesi Ngai. Ona Yesu ila wai munini, mutumia Simeoni niwatavisye Malia kana akewa kyeva kingi.
translation:
No!
God didn't fail.
Jesus hadn't made any mistake.
Jesus always knew He would be put to death by wicked men.
Even when Jesus was a baby,
an old man named Simeon had told Mary that sadness lay ahead.

text: Mithenya mivuthu mbee wa Yesu tanamba kuwawa, ve kiveti kuyookie na kyamwitikisya mauta maauni make. "Eananga mbesa." Amanyiwa manungunika. "Niwakuna wia museo." Yesu amatavya. "Akuna kii nundu wa mathiko makwa." Ndeto ngeni.
translation:
A few days before Jesus was killed,
a lady came and poured perfumed ointment on His feet.
"She's wasting money," the disciples complained.
"She's done a good work," Jesus said.
"She did it for my burial."
What strange words!

text: Itina wa uu, Yutasi umwe wa ala atume ikumi na eli ma Yesu, aamua kumuvuthania Yesu kwa muthembi munene kwa ilungu miongo itatu sya fedha (30).
translation:
After this,
Judas,
one of Jesus' twelve disciples,
agreed to betray Jesus to the chief priests for 30 pieces of silver.

text:
Mbokani ya Ayuti ya mwiso, Yesu niwaie leu wake wamuthya na atume make. Niwamatavisye maundu maingi ma ungaini na mawatho make kwa aala mamwendete. Naindi Yesu niwoosie mukate na kikombe nikana matonye kuisania. Usu wai ulililkanyo kana mwii wa Yesu na nthakame yake
yanaenganiwe ni kana itonye kuete
uekeo wa mathavu maitu.
translation:
At the Jewish Passover feast,
Jesus had His last meal with His disciples.
He told them wonderful things about God and His promises to those who love Him.
Then Jesus gave bread and a cup for them to share.
These were to remind them that Jesus' body and blood were given to bring forgiveness for sins.

text: Na indi Yesu atavya anyanye kana nikuvunyaniwa, na masemba muno. "Nyisa kuutia," Vetelo amwia Yesu, nzamba mbe wa kwasa nukungannania katatu.
translation:
Then Jesus told His friends that He would be betrayed,
and they would run away.
"I won't run away,"
Peter insisted.
"Before the rooster crows,
you will deny Me three times,"
Jesus said.

text: Utuku usu, Yesu niwaiendie kuvoya muundani wa Gethsemani. Atume ala mainake nimakwatiwe ni too na makoma. "Asa wakwa," Yesu niwavoyie, "…Mbetangia kikombe kii ki mbee wakwa, indi ti undu ngwenda indi nundu ukwenda."
translation:
Later that night,
Jesus went to pray in the Garden of Gethsemane.
The disciples who were with Him fell asleep.
"O My Father,"
Jesus prayed,"...
Let this cup pass from Me.
Nevertheless,
not as I will,
but as You will."

text: Mituki ona nguthu ya andu mokite muundani. Matongoetwe ni Yutasi, Yesu ndamatungithya indi vetelo niwatilile mundu umwe kutu. Oavinditye, Yesu niwakwakitie mundu usu kutu na amuvosya. Yesu niweesi kukwatwa kwake wai muvango wa Ngai na kwenda kwake.
translation:
Suddenly a mob marched into the garden,
led by Judas.
Jesus did not resist,
but Peter cut off a man's ear.
Quietly,
Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him.
Jesus knew His arrest was part of God's will.

text: Na nguthu ya andu yamutwaa Yesu nyumbani ya muthembi munene. Na atongoi ma Ayuti masya nonginya Yesu akwe. Vakuvi, Vetelo aungamite vakuvi na mwaki wa athukumi na kwiloela.
translation:
The mob took Jesus to the high priest's house.
There,
the Jewish leaders said Jesus should die.
Nearby,
Peter stood beside the servants' fire and watched.

text: Mala atatu andu namamukulilye Vetelo, "We ndunethya na Yesu?" Mala atatu Vetelo akaia, otondu Yesu wamutavitye. Vetelo ona niweyumanie na evita.
translation: Three times people stared at Peter and said, "You were with Jesus!" Three times Peter denied it, just as Jesus said he would. Peter even cursed and swore.

text: Na indi nzamba yasya. No ta wai wasya wa Yesu kwa Vetelo. Aililikana ndeto sya Yesu, Vetelo niwaieie na woo mwingi muno.
translation:
Just then, a rooster crowed.
It was like God's voice to Peter.
Remembering Jesus' words,
Peter wept bitterly.

text: Yutasi onake niwelililie nundu niwese yesu ndaina ivityo ona yimwe. Yutasi niwatungie ila ilungu miongo itatu sya manemane indi vai muthembi wasyosya.
translation:
Judas was sorry, too.
He knew Jesus was not guilty of any sin or crime.
Judas took back the 30 pieces of silver,
but the priests wouldn't take it.

text: Na indi Yutasi niwekisye ila mbesa nthi, naathi nza- na esusya we mwene.
translation:
Judas threw the money down,
went out
- and hanged himself.

text: Athembi nimamuetie Yesu mbee wa Vilato, gavana wa Roma. Na Vilato asya, "Ndinona ivityo ya mundu uu." Naindi nguthu ya aandu yaendea na kwasya kwa wasya munene, "Mwambe!! Mwambe!!."
translation:
The priests brought Jesus before Pilate,
the Roman governor.
Pilate said,
"I have found no fault in this Man."
But the mob kept crying,
"Crucify Him!
Crucify Him!"

text: Muminikilyo Vilato niwamutwiie Yesu kikwu. Asikali nimamukunie, mamumba mata uthyuni wake. Nimamuseuvisye ngovia ya miwa miasa na mamwikia mutwene wake. Na indi mamukuniaa misumaa ngelanyoni na akwa.
translation:
Finally Pilate gave in,
and sentenced Jesus to die on a cross.
The soldiers punched Jesus,
spit in His face,
and whipped Him.
They made a cruel crown of long sharp thorns and pressed it onto His head.
Then they nailed Him to a wooden cross to die.

text: Yesu niwesi kana akakwa kwisila nzia isu. Niweesi kana kikwu kyake kikaete uekeo wa mathavu kwa eka ma nai ala mamuikia. Ingei ili syambitwe vamwe na Yesu. Kimwe nichamuikie Yesu na kyathi ituni indi kila kingi kiyamuuikia.
translation:
Jesus always knew He would die that way.
He also knew that His death would bring forgiveness for sinners who put their trust in Him.
Two criminals were crucified beside Jesus.
One believed on Jesus- and went to Paradise.
The other didn't.

text: Itina wa kuthinwa vandu va masaa, Yesu asya, "Niwathela," na akwa. Wia wake wai muthelu. Anthathaie make nimoosie mwii wake na mauthika vandu kimbithini.
translation:
After hours of suffering, Jesus said,
"It is finished," and died.
His work was completed.
Friends buried Him in a private tomb.

text: Na indi asikali ma Roma nimaendie kusunga kala kavuli. Vayai mundu wai alika kana akaumala.
translation:
Then Roman soldiers sealed and guarded the tomb.
Now nobody could get in
- or out.

text: Keka uu niwo wai muminikilo wa ngewa ya Yesu, wiona ta vethya kyeva ata? Indi Ngai niweekie kindu kya vata muno nundu Yesu ndaikala imukwu.
translation:
If this were the end of the story,
how sad it would be.
But God did something wonderful.
Jesus did not stay dead!

text: Kwakya tene muthenya wa mbee wa kyumwa, amanyiwa amwe ma yesu nimeethie ivia yila yavingite kavuli kake yumitwe. Yila masyaisye nthini mayamwona Yesu.
translation:
Early in the morning of the first day of the week,
some of Jesus' disciples found the stone rolled away from the grave.
When they looked inside,
Jesus was no longer there.

text: Kiveti kimwe nikyekalile mbuani kiyiiya lakini Yesu akyumilia!! Nichasembie na muyo na kyathi kutavya amanyiwa make atii, "NIMUTHAYAUUKU!! NUTHAYUUKIE KUMA KWA AKWU!"
translation:
One woman stayed,
weeping by the tomb.
Jesus appeared to her!
She rushed back joyfully to tell the other disciples.
"JESUS IS ALIVE!
JESUS HAS COME BACK FROM THE DEAD!"

text: Mituki yesu niwookie vala vai amanyaiwa make na amonya moko make kula misumaa yatonyaa. Niwo, YESU NIMUTHAYUUKU!! Niwaiekie Vetelo nundu wa umukakanisya, na atavya atume matavye andu iulu wa kuthayuuka kwake. Na indi asyuka ituni oo kula waumite.
translation:
Soon Jesus came to the disciples,
and showed them His nail-scarred hands.
It was true.
JESUS WAS ALIVE AGAIN!
He forgave Peter for denying Him,
and told His disciples to tell everybody about Him.
Then He went back to heaven where He had come from.

text:
Easter Yambee
Ngewa kuma kwa ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia
Yonekanaa
Mathayao 26-28, Luka 22-24, Yohana 13-21
"Kulika kwa ndeto yaku kũetae kyeni."
Savulĩ 119:130
translation:
The First Easter
A story from God's Word, the Bible, is found in
Matthew 26-28; Luke 22-24; John 13-21
"
The entrance of Your Words gives light.
"
Psalm 119:130

text:
Tene muno, Ngai niwatumie mulaika Ngavulileli kula kwi kelitu kanini kuma yuta ketawa malia. Na amutavya, ukeethya na kana ka kavisi na isitya yako ukaketa Yesu. Na akeetwa mwana wa ual wiyiulu na akasumbukia
tene na tene.
translation:
Long ago,
God sent the angel Gabriel to a sweet young Jewish maiden named Mary.
He told her,
"You will have a son and call His Name Jesus.
He will be called the Son of the Highest.
He will reign forever."

text: "Undu uu ukatonyeka ata?" Kelitu malia kasengete muno kakulya. "Ndimwisi muundu ume." Na mulaika amwia kana kakauma kula kwi Ngai. Kaikethiwa na ithe wa kiimundu.
translation:
"How can this be?"
the amazed girl asked.
"I have not been with any man."
The angel told Mary the child would come from God.
There would not be a human father.

text: Na mulaika asyoka amutavya Malia kana mwendwa wake Elisaveti ni muito. O kavinda kanini, Malia athi kwa Elisaveti na mathaitha vamwe.
translation:
The angel then told Mary that her cousin Elizabeth was having a baby in her old age.
This was a miracle, too.
Soon after,
Mary visited Elizabeth.
They praised God together.

text: Malia niweevaawa ni mundu wetawa Yosevu. Na Yosevu niweewie woo yila wethie Malia ee muito. Asuaniia kana aitaviwe ni muundu ume ungi.
translation:
Mary was engaged to marry a man named Joseph.
Joseph was sad when he learned Mary was expecting a baby.
He thought some other man was the father.

text: Ndotoni, mulaika wa Mwaia amumilila Yosevu an amutavya kaan ni ka Ngai. Na indi Yosevu niwatetheeisye Malia kusuvia kan yesu.
translation:
In a dream,
God's angel told Joseph that this child was God's Son.
Joseph was to help Mary look after Jesus.

text: Yosevu ae muikikiku na kumwiwa Ngai. Niwaatia miao ya nthi yake. Nundu wa mwiao mweu, we na Malia nimaumia musyi munene ula mekalaa, Mbethelemu, makaive koti.
translation:
Joseph trusted and obeyed God.
He also obeyed his country's laws.
Because of a new law,
he and Mary left for their hometown, Bethlehem,
to pay their taxes.

text: Yosevu ae muikikiku na kumwiwa Ngai. Niwaatia miao ya nthi yake. Nundu wa mwiao mweu, we na Malia nimaumia musyi munene ula mekalaa, Mbethelemu, makaive koti.
translation:
Mary was ready to have her baby.
But Joseph could not find a room anywhere.
All the inns were full.

text: Muthya Yosevu niwakwatie vandu kituuni. Vau nivo kana Yesu kasyaiwe, inya niwakakomisye muvalatini, vala indo syanengeawa leu.
translation:
Joseph finally found a stable.
There,
Baby Jesus was born.
His mother laid Him in a manger,
a place where the animals' food was usually put.

text:
Ovakuvi na vala aithi masungaa indo syoo ikomete. Mulaika wa Mwaia niwamaumiliile na amatavya
ndeto isu nzeo.
translation:
Nearby, shepherds guarded their sleeping flocks.
God's angel appeared and told them the wonderful news.

text:
"Umunthi nusyaiwe mwovosya musyini wa Ndaviti. Ula niwe Yesu Klisto na mwiithia kana kakomete
muvalatini."
translation:
"There is born to you this day in the city of David a Savior Who is Christ the Lord.
You will find the Baby lying in a manger."

text:
Mituki alaika aingi maumila me akenuku ta kyeni.
Maitaia Mwaia na mayasya, "Ukumyo kwa Ngai
iulu Ituni na vaa nthi kwa andu ma
wendo museo."
translation:
Suddenly,
many more bright angels appeared,
praising God and saying,
"Glory to God in the Highest and
on earth peace, good will toward men."

text:
Na aithi kwa mituki mokila makakone kaukenge. Na indi mamina kukona nimasyokie na kutavya kila umwe makomana undu mulaika wamatavisye iulu wa yesu
mwovosya.
translation:
The shepherds hurried to the stable.
After seeing the Baby they told everyone they met what the angels had said about Jesus.

text: Itina wa mithenya miongo ina, Yosevu na Malia ni maetie yesu ikaluni kuya yelesulame. Vai mundu weetawa Simioni ula wataaie Ngai aimukatha nundu wa kana Yesu. Anna muthukumi ungi wa Ngai niwatungie muvea.
translation:
Forty days later,
Joseph and Mary brought Jesus to the temple in Jerusalem.
There a man named Simeon praised God for the Baby,
while old Anna,
another servant of the Lord,
gave thanks.

text: Meeli nimamanyie kana Yesu ni mwana wa Ngai mvovosya ula wai mwathane. Yosevu niwaumisye nyunyi ili. Syindu isu ni Mwiao ula Ngai waumitye waasya. Andu ala nja maele kuetea Mwia yila kana kasyawa.
translation:
Both knew Jesus was God's Son,
the promised Savior.
Joseph sacrificed two birds.
This was the offering God's law said poor people should bring when they presented a newborn child to
the Lord.

text: Itinanga vanini, ndata ya mwanya niyatongoisye andu atatu kuma umiloni wa sua kuka Yelusaleme. "Ai va ula usyaiwe musumbi wa Ayuti?" Makulya. "Tuenda kumuthaitaha."
translation:
Sometime later,
a special star led Wise Men from an Eastern country to Jerusalem.
"Where is He Who is born King of the Jews?" they asked.
"We want to worship Him."

text: Yila musumbi Elote weewie uvoo wa anadu atatu oi, niwanyamaikie muno na amakulya mamutavye vala kana Yesu kasyaiwe. "Nienda uthi ukathaitha." Eleto aasya. Lakini niwakenganaa. Elote eenda kuwaa kana Yesu.
translation:
King Herod heard about the Wise Men.
Troubled, he asked them to tell him when they found Jesus.
"I want to worship Him, too,"
Herod said.
But he was lying.
Herod wanted to kill Jesus.

text: Na indi ndata yamatongoesya andu oi nginya nyumba ila yai Malia na Yosevu mena Kana Yesu. Nimatulilye ndu makathaitha na manenga Yesu mithinzio ya thaavu, uvumba na manemane.
translation:
The star led the Wise Men to the exact house where Mary and Joseph lived with the young Child.
Kneeling in worship,
the travelers gave Jesus rich gifts of gold and perfume.

text: Na indi Ngai amakanya andu oi mambia kwinuka menuke kimbithine nundu Elote aina woo mwingi. Eyumbanasya kumuaa Yesu. Niwaisye syana syoonthe sya imwana syuwawe na syowawa Mbethelemu.
translation:
God warned the Wise Men to return home secretly.
Herod was furious.
Determined to destroy Jesus,
the wicked ruler killed all boy babies in Bethlehem.

text: Indi Elote nda Kooa kana ka Ngai! Yosevu na Malia nimakaniwe ndotoni matwaie kana Yesu usuvioni nthi ya Misili.
translation:
But Herod could not harm God's Son!
Warned in a dream,
Joseph took Mary and Jesus to safety in Egypt.

text:
Yila elote wakwie, Yosevu
niwamutungie Malia na kana Yesu kuma
Misili. Maendie kwikala musyi munini wa
Nazaleti. Vakuvi na ukanga wa Ngalilaya.
translation:
When Herod died Joseph brought
Mary and Jesus back from Egypt.
They lived in
the little town of Nazareth,
near the sea of Galilee.

text:
Kusyawa kwa Yesu
Ngewa kuma kwa ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia
Yonekanaa
Mathayo 1- 2, Luka 1- 2
"Kulika kwa ndeto yaku kũetae kyeni."

The Birth of Jesus
A story from God's Word, the Bible, is found in

"

text: Noah niwekalaa aivoya ngai ula andu ala angi onthe nimamenete na kulea kumwiwa Ngai. Muthenya umwe, Ngai niwanenie undu wa kutelemya na asya,
translation:
Noah was a man who worshiped God.
Everyone else hated and disobeyed God.
One day, God said something shocking.

text: "Ngaananga nthi ino ya iema ," Ngai atavya Noah. "No uwe na musyi waku ukatangiiwa."
translation:
"I will destroy this wicked world,"
God told Noah.
"Only your family will be saved."

text: Na ngai atavya Noah kana kiwu kingi nikikuka na kuvyuka nthi. "Seuvya ngalawa ya muti (miti). Isiwa inene muno yitonya kulika musyi waku na nyamu mbingi."
translation:
God warned Noah that a great flood would come and cover the earth.
"Build a wooden ark,
a boat big enough for your family and many animals,"
Noah was
ordered.

text: Noah atavwa ni Ngai. Ngai amutavya undu ukwika na indi Noah aambia wia.
translation: God gave Noah exact instructions. Noah got busy!

text: Na indi andu maambia kumuvuthya. Na Noah amatavya kitumi kya kwaka ngalawa.
translation: Probably people mocked as Noah explained why he was making an ark.

text: Na Noah aendeea na kwaka na aendeea na kumatavya andu ndeto sya Ngai. Vai mundu ona umwe waaiwa kana kumwithukiisya.
translation:
Noah kept building.
He also kept telling people about God.
Nobody listened.

text: Noah aina muikiio munene. Niwaikiaa Ngai onethwa mbua ndiambite kua. Na indi ngalawa yathela Noah ambililya kulikya miio.
translation:
Noah had great faith.
He believed God even though rain had never fallen before.
Soon the ark was ready to be loaded with supplies.

text: Nayu tuke nyamu, Ngai aete mithemba muonza ya syo, na ingi ili sya mithemba ingi. Nyunyi nene na nini, tunyamu tula tunini na ila nene, syambia kulika ngalawani.
translation:
Now came the animals.
God brought seven of some species,
two of others.
Birds great and small,
beasts tiny and tall made their way to the ark.

text:
Nayu andu maambia kumuumanga Noah
aendee kulikya
nyamu. Mayaeeka
kumuvitisya . . .
translation:
Perhaps the people shouted insults at Noah as he loaded the animals.
They did
not stop sinning
against God.
They
did not ask to
enter the ark.

text:
. . . Ngai kwa mathavu moo na mayaakulya
Noah kulika
ngalawani.
translation:
Perhaps the people shouted insults at Noah as he loaded the animals.
They did
not stop sinning
against God.
They
did not ask to
enter the ark.

text: Muthya, nyamu syoonthe na nyunyi nisyalikilwe ngalawani. "Uka ngalawani," Ngai eeta Noah. "We na musyi waku." Noah, muka wake, syana syake syi itatu na iveti syoo malika ngalawani, Na Ngai avunga muomo.
translation:
Finally, all the animals and
birds were aboard.
"Come
into the ark,"
God invited
Noah.
"You and your family."
Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives entered the ark.
Then God shut the door!

text: Na indi mbua yaambia. Mbua nene yetika yavyika nthi vandu va matuku miongo ina na utuku.
translation:
Then the rain came.
A great downpour soaked the earth for forty days and nights.

text: Kiwu kyausua kyavyika misyoi na ndua. Yila mbua yaungamie, ona iima syavyikitwe ni kiwu. Kila kindu kyoonthe kivevaa nzeve ni kyakwie.
translation:
Floodwaters poured over towns and villages.
When the rain stopped,
even the mountains were under water.
Everything that breathed air died.

text: Yila kiwu kyambatie, ngalawa ni yalelie yiulu. Nivatonyeka kwithiwa na kivindu nthini, kwithiwa na utulu na kana kutelema. Lakini ngalawa niyasie Noah kukuwa ni kiwu.
translation:
As the waters rose,
the ark floated on top.
It may have been dark inside,
maybe bumpy,
maybe even scary.
But the ark sheltered Noah from the flood.

text:
Itina wa mwei itano ya kiwu kingi, Ngai niwatumie kiseve kya unyasya. Kavola ngalawa niyookie kukoomea kiima iulu kya Ararat. Noah niwasyokie
ekala mithenya ingi miongo ina ngalawani kiwu
kithele.
translation:
After five months of flooding,
God sent a drying wind.
Slowly,
the ark came to rest high in the mountains of Ararat.
Noah stayed inside another forty days as the water lowered.

text: Noah niwatumie Raven na ivui nza wa ngalawa avingua ndilisya na syeethia vai vandu vaseo vanyau itonya kwikala. Na ivui yasyoka vale ve Noah.
translation:
Noah sent a raven and a dove out of the ark's open window.
Not finding a dry,
clean place to rest,
the dove returned to Noah.

text:
Itina wa kyumwa kimwi, noah atata ingi. Ivui niyookie yikuite itu na munuka wayo. Kyumwa kila kyaatie, noah ni wamanyie kana nthi ninyau ndu
ivui yiyaasyoka.
translation:
A week later,
Noah tried again.
The dove came back with a new olive leaf in its beak.
The next week Noah knew the earth was dry
because the dove
did not return.

text: Na indi Ngai amwia Noah, ni ivinda ya kuma ngalawani. Noah vamwe na andu make mambililya kumya nyamu.
translation:
God told Noah it was time to leave the ark.
Together,
Noah and his family unloaded the animals.

text: Noah two ta weewie unene!! Niwaakie kithembeo na a, uthaiytha Ngai ula wamutangiie vamwe na nyumba yake kumanwa na mbua nene.
translation:
How grateful Noah must have felt!
He built an altar and worshiped God Who had saved him and his family from the awful flood.

text: Ngai niwanengie Noah watho museo amwia, vai sua ungi ngatumia mbua nene kusilila mundu. Ngai anengana ulilikanwo munene wa watho wake.
translation:
God gave Noah a wonderful promise.
Never again would He send a flood to judge human sin.

text: Na indi utathi niwo ngelekanyo ya watho wa Ngai ula waathanie.
translation:
God gave a great reminder of His promise.
The rainbow was the sign of God's promise.

text: Itina wa kiwu kingi Noah na musyi wake nimaambililye mwambililyo mweu. Nziawa syonthe sya nthi syaumia vala ve Noah na syana syake.
translation:
Noah and his family found new beginnings after the flood.
In time,
his descendants re-peopled the whole earth.
All the nations of the world came from Noah and his children.

text:
Noah na kiwu kingi

Noah and the Great Flood

text: Ngai niwoombie kila kindu!! Yila Ngai woombie mundu wa mbee, Adam, ekalaa muundani wa eden ena muka wake, Hawa. Mai alungalu mayiatiia mioa ya ngai na kutania kwithiwa kwake nginya muthenya umwe …
translation:
GOD MADE EVERYTHING!
When God made the first man, Adam,
he lived in the Garden of Eden with his wife,
Eve.
They were perfectly happy obeying God and enjoying His presence until one day...

text: "Ngai niwakwiie nduakaye kila muti?" Nzoka yakulya Hawa. "Notuye kila mutunda ate umwe." Asungia. "Yila tuya kana kukwata mutunda usu, nituukwa," Muikwa, nzoka yamukenga.
translation:
"Did God tell you not to eat of every tree?" the serpent asked Eve.
"We can eat of every fruit but one,"
she replied.
"If we eat or touch that fruit,
we will die."
"You won't die,"
the serpent smirked.

text: "Mwiikala ta ngai" na Hawa endeewa ni matunda ma muti usu. Ethukisya nzoka na aya itunda.
translation:
"You'll become like God."
Eve wanted the fruit of that tree.
She listened to the serpent and ate the fruit.

text: Hawa amina kumivitisya Ngai niwa mutongoesye Adam kuay itunda onake. Adam aile kwasya "aye" ndileana na ndeto sya Ngai.
translation:
After Eve disobeyed God she led Adam to eat the fruit also.
Adam should have said,
"No!
I will not disobey God's Word."

text: Mamina kumuvitisya Ngai Adam na Hawa, ni mamanyie kana ni athei, nimatumanisye matu ma kivuti na miiwa, nimeevyikie na meevitha kithekani ni kana Ngai ndakamone.
translation:
When Adam and Eve sinned,
they both knew they were naked.
Sewing fig leaves into aprons,
they covered themselves and hid in the bush from God's presence.

text: Kwa usya yiawiyoo Ngai ooka muundani. Niweesi undu Adam na Hawa mekie. Adam ambia kumutula mutu Hawa. Nake Hawa amitula muti nzoka. Ngai asya, "Nzoka niwamiumania. Na mundu muka akewaa woo mwingi aisyaa."
translation:
In the cool of the evening God came to the garden.
He knew what Adam and Eve had done.
Adam blamed Eve.
Eve blamed the serpent.
God said, "The serpent is cursed.
The woman will have pain when children are born."

text: "Adam na nundu nuvitisye, nthi niyaumaniwa na miwa na wauni utakathelaa. Ukang'ang'ana na kunyala uikwata kya kuya(liu)."
translation:
"Adam,
because you sinned,
the earth is cursed with thorns and thistles.
You will toil and sweat to get your daily food."

text: Ngai niwamalungilye Adam na Hawa muundani usu mwailu, nundu wa kuvitya. Nimaatanisye na Ngai ula unenganae thayu.
translation:
God put Adam and Eve out of the wonderful garden.
Because they sinned,
they were separated from the life-giving God!

text: Ngai niwaseuvisye umui wa uvyu wa na amavetanga nza wa muunda wa eden. Na Ngai aseuvya ikoti ya kithuma ya Adanm na Hawa. Ngai aumisye kithuma va?
translation:
God made a flaming sword to keep them out.
God made coats of skin for Adam and Eve.
Where did God take the skins from?

text: Saani isu, musyi niwasyaiwe ni Adam na Hawa. Mwana woo wa mbee muundume eetwa kaini, na ai undu wa muundani. Mwana woo wa keli muundume eetwa Aveli na ai muithi.
translation:
In time,
a family was born to Adam and Eve.
Their first son,
Cain,
was a gardener.
Their second son,
Abel,
was a shepherd.

text: Muthenya umwe Kaini aetea Ngai mboka ta muthinzio. Aveli nake aetea Ngai kalondu kake kala kae kaseo muno vyu tawo muthinzio wake. Na Ngai niweendeewie muno ni thembo ya Aveli.
translation:
One day Cain brought God some vegetables as a gift.
Abel brought some of the very best of his sheep as his gift to God.
God was pleased with Abel's gift.

text: Ngai ndaendewa ni nthembo ya kaini. Kaini niwewie woo mwingi muno. Na Ngai asya "Weeka undu vaile, nulea kwitikilwa?"
translation:
God was not pleased with Cain's gift.
Cain got very angry.
But God said,
"If you do what is right,
will you not be accepted?"

text: Woo wa Kaini uyaathi mana. Ivinda yimwe itina kuya wiini niwamuvithukie Aveli na amuaa.
translation:
Cain's anger didn't go away.
Some time later in the field he attacked Abel
- and killed him!

text: Na Ngai aneena na Kaini. "Aiva mwanaa mwnyu, Aveli?" "Ndyisi," Kaini akengana. Akulya "niinye niia mwana mwaitu Aveli?" Ngai niwamwonisye ukuno munene kwa kwosa umanthi ula wamunengete wa uimi na amutwikithya musungi.
translation:
God spoke to Cain.
"Where is your brother,
Abel?"
"I don't know,"
Cain lied.
"Am I my brother's keeper?"
God punished Cain by taking away his ability to farm and making him a wanderer.

text: Kaini niwaiendie nza wa muamba na Mwiai. Na niwatwaie mwiitu wa wa Adam na Hawa na mamesya musyi.
translation:
Cain went out from the presence of the LORD.
He was married to a daughter of Adam and Eve.
They raised a family.

text: O mituki esukuee na nganana sya Kaini syaususya musyi ula waambiie.
translation:
Soon,
Cain's grandchildren and great-grandchildren filled the city that he founded.

text: Kilungu o kinini nyumba ya Adam na Hawa yeana o mituku. Mithenya isu andu mekala muno kuthonoka umunthi.
translation:
Meanwhile,
the family of Adam and Eve grew quickly.
In those days,
people lived much longer than today.

text: Yila mwana woo muundume Seth wasyaiwe, Hawa aisye, "Ngai anengie Seth nikenda atungie Aveli." Seth ai mundu wa Ngai ula wekalile miaka 912 na aina syana mbingi.
translation:
When her son Seth was born,
Eve said,
"God gave me Seth to replace Abel."
Seth was a godly man who lived 912 years and had many children.

text:
Nthini wa nthi, Andu nimaendeeie kwithiwa na woseeku
kuma nzyawa kuthi ila ingi.
Mumimikilyo, Ngai niwasuanie
kumina mundu Nyamu syonthe
na nyunyi …
translation:
In the world,
people became more and more wicked as one generation followed another.
Finally,
God decided to destroy mankind and...

text: Ngai elila nundu wa kumba mundu. Lakini mundu umwe amwendeesya Ngai …
translation:
...all beasts and birds.
God was sorry he had made man.
But one man pleased God...

text: Mundu uyu etawa Noah, nzia ya Seth, Noah ai mutheu na mulungalu. Aendanasya na Ngai.
translation:
This man was Noah.
A descendent of Seth,
Noah was righteous and blameless.
He walked with God.

text: Ni wavundiisye syana syake syi itatu kumwiwa Ngai. Na indi Ngai avanga kutumia Noah kwa nzia ya ueni na ya mwanya.
translation:
He also taught his three sons to obey God.
Now God planned to use Noah in a very strange and special way!

text:
Mwambililyo wa mindu kwiwa woo (kyeva)
Ngewa kuma kwa ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia
Yonekanaa
Mwambililyo 3 – 6
"Kulika kwa ndeto yaku kũetae kyeni."
Savulĩ 119:130
translation:
The Start of Man's Sadness
A story from God's Word, the Bible, is found in
Genesis 3 to 6
"
The entrance of Your Words gives light.
"
Psalm 119:130

text:
Nuu waatumbie? Mbivilia ndeto ya Ngai, yitutavya undu mundu woombiwe. Tene muno, Ngai niwoombie mundu wa mbee na amwita Adam. Ngai niwoombie Adam kuma muthangani wa nthi.
Yila Ngai waveveeie Adam veva, niweethiiwena thayu na
eyithia ee mundane mwanake
wa Eden.
translation:
Who made us?
The Bible, God's Word, tells how the human race began.
Long ago, God made the very first man and named him Adam.
God made Adam out of the dust of the earth.
When God
breathed life into Adam, he came alive.
He found himself in
a beautiful garden called Eden.

text: Ngai atanamba kumba Adam, niwoombie nthi mbanake yusuitwe ni syindu mbanake (nzeo). Itambia kwa yingi Ngai niwoombie iima na kundu kutindimalu, malaa manake na iti (miti) ndaasa, nyunyi syina mawia manake (makenuku) na nzuki sya mwatuni, mikunga ya mbusini
translation:
Before God made Adam,
He made a beautiful world filled with wonderful things.
Step by step God made hilly places and prairie spaces,
fragrant flowers and tall trees,
brightly-feathered birds and buzzing bees,
wallowing whales and slippery snails.

text: na manyonga matendeu. Wo, Ngai ombie kila kindu ve kila kindu.
translation:
In fact,
God made everything there is – everything.

text: Kuma Mwambililyo, Mbee wa Ngai atanamba kumba kindu, vayai kindu kingi ate Ngai. Vayai andu kana kindu kana syindu. Vaikindu. Kuyai kyeni kana kivindu, kuyai iulu kana nthi. Kuyai iyoo kana uni. No Ngai waivo ula ute mwambililyo. Na Ngai ambiia.
translation:
In the very beginning,
before God made anything,
there was nothing except God.
No people or places or things.
Nothing.
No light and no darkness.
No up and no down.
No yesterday and no tomorrow.
There was only God Who had no beginning.
Then God acted!

text: Mwambililyo Ngai niwoombie itu na nthi.
translation: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

text: Na nthi ndyaina kindu. Na kivindu kyai ngaliko ya uliku, na Ngai asya "Nikwithiwe nKyeni".
translation:
And the earth was without form and void.
And darkness was on the face of the deep.
Then God spoke.
"Let there be light."

text: Na kyeni kyeethiwa. Na Ngai eeta kyeni muthenya na kivindu akita utuku. Na iawithoo na kwakya kwethewa muthenya wa mbee.
translation:
And there was light.
God called the light Day and the darkness He called Night.
And the evening and the morning were the first day.

text: Muthenya wa keli, Ngai niweetie kiwu kya ukanga, yiia, uungu wa itu. Muthenya wa katatu, Ngai asya, "kwithiwe nthi numu." Na kweethiwa.
translation:
On the second day, God brought the waters of the oceans, seas and lakes into order under Heaven.
On the third day, God said, "Let the dry land appear."
And it happened.

text: Ngai asyoka asya nyeki na malaa na miti ya uiini na miti ya kithekani ni yithiwe. Na kweethiwa.
translation:
God also commanded the grass and flowers and shrubs and trees
to appear.
And they appeared.

text: Na iawiyoo na kwakya kwethya muthenya wa katatu.
translation: And the evening and the morning were the third day.

text: Na Ngai oomba sua, na mwai, na ndata mbingi ila mundu utatala. Na wiyoo na kwakya kwetha muthenya wa kana.
translation:
Then God made the sun, and the moon, and so many stars that nobody can count them.
And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.

text: Tusamu twa ukangani na makuyu na nyunyi nisyo syaatie muvangoni wa Ngai. Muthenya wa katano ni woombie makuyu ala manene na syingelete, nyaa syi maau masa na tusuni tunini. Ngai oomba kila muthemba wa makuyukususya kiwu kya nthi na kila muthemba wa nyunyi itonye kutania nthi, na ukanga na thayayani. Na iawiyoo na kwakya kweethiwa muthenya wa katano.
translation:
Sea creatures and fish and birds were next on God's list.
On the fifth day He made big swordfish and tiny sardines,
long-legged ostriches and happy little humming birds.
God made every kind of fish to fill earth's waters and every kind of bird to enjoy the land and sea and sky.
And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.

text: Itina wa uu Ngai aasya ingi, Asya, "nthi ni yiete kyumbe kya kana..." Kila muthemba wa nyamu na tusamu na ila syi makwau ta ingangi syeethiwa. Kweethiwa na nzou na nzuki sya kithekani. Nyamu syonthe syoombiwe ni ngai muthenya usu. Na iawiyoo na kwakya niwo wai muthenya wa nthantatu.
translation:
After that,
God spoke again.
He said,
"Let the earth bring forth living creatures . . ."
Every kind of animal and insect and reptile came into being.
There were earth-shaking elephants and busy beavers.
Mischievous monkeys and clumsy crocodiles.
Wiggly worms and cheeky chipmunks.
Gangly giraffes and purring pussy cats.
Every kind of animal was made by God that day.
And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

text: Ngai niweekie undu ungi muthenya wa nthanthatu. Kila kindu kyai kianiu munduni. Vai leu muundani na nyamu sya umuthukuma. Na ngai asya "Ekai tumbe mundu kwa muvyano witu. Eka ethywe ee munene kana muungamiie wa kila kindu iulu wa nthi."
translation:
God did something else on the sixth day - something very special.
Everything was now ready for Man.
There was food in the fields and animals to serve him.
And God said,
"Let Us make man in Our image.
Let him be lord over everything on the earth."

text: KWOU NGAI OMBOIE MUNDU KWA MUVYANO WAKE, KWA MUVYANO WAKE NI WA MUMBIE.
translation: SO GOD CREATED MAN IN HIS OWN IMAGE; IN THE IMAGE OF GOD HE CREATED HIM...

text: Ngai niwaninie na Adam. "Ya kila ukwenda muundani uu, ate ndukaye mutini ula wa umanyi wa useo na uthuku. Woona waya mutini usu kwawo ukakwa."
translation:
God spoke to Adam.
"Eat what you wish from the garden.
But do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
If you eat from that tree you will surely die."

text:
Na mwia Ngai aasya, "Ti useo mundu ekale eweka. Ningumumbia mutetheesya." Na ngai aete nyunyi syonthe na nyamu sya kithekani kula kwi Adam. Na Adam ainenga masyitwa syoonthe. No nginya aena ui mwingi muno wa kwika uu. Indi oou wivo nthini wa nyunyi na nyamu vayai ithiwa
na mutindania ula waile kwikalanya na Adam.
translation:
And the LORD God said,
"It is not good that man should be alone.
I will make a helper for him."
God brought all the birds and beasts to Adam.
Adam named them all.
He must have been very clever to do so.
But among all the birds and beasts there was no suitable partner for Adam.

text: Ngai aete Adam nthini wa too munene, munene muno. Na aumya uwau umwe wake ee too. Na Ngai oomba mundu muka kuma uwauni wa Adam. Na indi, mundu muka ula Ngai woombie ethiwa emwailu kwikalanasya na Adam.
translation:
God brought Adam into a deep, deep sleep.
Removing one of the sleeping man's ribs,
God formed Woman from Adam's rib.
The woman God made was exactly right to be a partner for Adam.

text: Ngai niwaminie kumba kila kindu muthenya wa nthanthatu, na indi Ngai aathima muthenya wa muonza na autwikithya muthenya wa kuthumuua. Kuya muundani wa eden, Adam na muka wake Hawa maina mwambililyo museo wa utanu na kumwiwa mwiaa Ngai woo, mumanyi woo na munyanyae woo.
translation:
God made everything in six days.
Then God blessed the seventh day and made it a day of rest.
In the garden of Eden,
Adam and Eve his wife had perfect happiness obeying God.
God was their LORD,
their Provider and their Friend.
